originality.rationale: Inspected primary circular-cone work supplies projection/generalized derivative formulas but does not state or imply, without new row-norm optimization, the two scalar sharp coordinatewise moduli and their globally optimized high-dimensional aperture law. The closest published endpoint-stability result covers only the unscaled Lorentz case; the earlier planar scaled-cone result uses a different input/output metric. No directly equivalent all-aperture all-dimensional asymptotic law was found. Historical-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: A previously unknown equivalent optimization of generalized circular-cone Jacobians may exist in older conic sensitivity or operator-norm literature.
Finite-dimensional exact optimal slopes or crossover curves are not determined by this theorem; comparison is of the dimension-normalized asymptotic.
Coordinatewise robustness depends on fixing the cone axis along the first coordinate; arbitrary rotations are not covered.

value.rationale: Beyond a bare projection derivative, the theorem solves a natural exact coordinatewise robustness problem to two scalar maximizations and proves uniform-in-aperture minimax growth, with distinct reciprocal optimal cone slopes and a three-mechanism transition. It supplies a principled scale-sensitive robustness budget for nonsymmetric circular-cone projection.
